sources.entry: Janus - General-purpose, lightweight, minimalist WebRTC Server. (Demo, Source Code) GPL-3.0 C

summary.one_liner: Janus is an open source, general-purpose WebRTC server developed by Meetecho, tailored for Linux (with macOS support) and built from C with a plugin architecture.
summary.what_it_does: Janus is a WebRTC server that handles WebRTC media and signaling through a core plus pluggable modules. The README describes plugins for SIP, AudioBridge (Opus audio mixing), Streaming, recordings post-processing, and Lua, Duktape, and sample Event Handler plugins. The core can be controlled through an HTTP REST API, and optionally through WebSockets, MQTT, RabbitMQ, or Nanomsg, and it can emit events to those transports. It supports optional Data Channels (via usrsctp), ICE Lite, ICE-TCP, TURN REST API support, NAT 1:1 configuration, and RTP port ranges. Configuration is via a jcfg file or command-line options, and the repo includes HTML demo pages in an html folder for testing.
use_cases: audio conference bridge with Opus mixing
stream RTP or RTSP media to browsers
notable: Plugin architecture with SIP, AudioBridge, Streaming, Lua, and Duktape plugins
Multiple control transports: HTTP REST, WebSockets, MQTT, RabbitMQ, Nanomsg
Built-in demo pages in the html folder for testing
caveats: Windows is not supported; it only works under Windows Subsystem for Linux, and the README warns against unofficial .exe builds
Many optional dependencies must be installed manually (libnice, libsrtp 2.x, usrsctp, libwebsockets, rabbitmq-c), and the README recommends building some from source
FreeBSD note: rtp_forward only works when streaming to IPv6
